functions.get_item(sku: str) -> dict | None: returns {"sku": str, "name": str, "price": float (dollars, e.g. 12.5 = $12.50), "category": str}; None if sku unknown
functions.get_customer(customer_id: str) -> dict |: returns {"id": str, "name": str, "discount": float (fraction, 0.10 = 10%), "region": str}; None if unknown

why: Team standard: money in float dollars, percentages as fractions, lookups return None. Data stored as price_cents and discount_pct is converted at load time.

value.lines: list of dicts {"category": str, "amount_cents": int}; amount_cents = line total before discount, integer cents, >= 0. Caller (invoice.py) builds it from pricing.py data.
value.region: customer region code such as "TX", "NY", "OR" (must match data_tax/rates.csv). Pass None for an unknown customer; None means tax 0 and no error. A non-None region not in rates.csv raises KeyError.
value.discount_pct: customer discount as a percent number (e.g. 10 for 10%). Pass 0 if no discount. Taken from pricing.py.
value.category_rule: a line whose category is listed in data_tax/exempt_categories.csv (currently: food) is not taxed. Any other category, including unknown ones, is taxable.
value.return: tax amount as integer cents, rounded half up. tax.py never returns a float.
value.formula: taxable = sum of amount_cents for taxable lines; base = taxable * (100 - discount_pct) / 100 (exact, not rounded); tax = base * rate_pct / 100, rounded half up to the cent. invoice.py adds tax to the subtotal; it does not compute tax itself.
value.other_functions: tax.tax_rate(region) -> float percent (KeyError if unknown; None returns 0). Optional helper for display only.

why: Proposal for the tax.py API, following the team standard (integer cents, percent numbers, KeyError on lookup miss). Mainly needs agent1 (pricing supplies category/discount) and agent3 (invoice calls sales_tax) to accept.

Conflicts with our team standard (agent1): money = float dollars, percentages = fractions, lookup miss = None. Proposed counter: tax.sales_tax(lines, region, discount) where lines = [{category, amount}] with amount = float dollars (pre-discount line total), discount = fraction from pricing (0.10 = 10%), region = code or None; returns float dollars rounded half-up to the cent (use Decimal internally). Unknown region raises KeyError or returns None, your choice, but please document it. Category exemptions and the formula are fine as written. If you cannot adopt floats, tell me and I will convert at my boundary instead; I will not change pricing_api.
superseded by v2 with boundary conversion in invoice.py (answers agent1 objection)

why: v2: keeps the team standard inside tax.py (integer cents, percent numbers, KeyError) so tax math is exact. agent1 keeps pricing_api unchanged; the unit conversion happens once in invoice.py at the call site. Answers agent1 objection: unknown region raises KeyError, documented.
v2 accepted by agent1. pricing_api unchanged; the cents/percent conversion at the invoice.py call site is fine for my module.

agent3 accepts pricing_api v1 as proposed. invoice.py converts price float dollars to integer cents via Decimal(repr(price)) and treats None as unknown SKU / unknown customer. Discount fraction is converted to a percent number (x100) at the call site.
